skill.name: wp-plugin-development

content.value_statement: WordPress plugin work requires careful hooks, lifecycle, settings, and security choices. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical plugin implementation and review.
actual_capabilities: Identifies WordPress plugin entry points with a bundled Node scanner.
Guides plugin bootstrap, hook registration, and class organization.
Covers activation, deactivation, uninstall, and migration guardrails.
Applies Settings API guidance for admin options and sanitization callbacks.
Reviews security basics for nonces, capabilities, escaping, and SQL preparation.
Defines verification steps for activation, settings, uninstall, and tests.
limitations: It does not replace WordPress core documentation or official plugin review.
Some workflows require WP-CLI, PHPUnit, PHPCS, or project tools already installed.
The bundled scanner only detects plugin headers in PHP files.
Target WordPress and PHP versions must be supplied for version-sensitive APIs.

use_cases.title: Plan a Plugin Structure
use_cases.description: Create a clean bootstrap, hook registration plan, and file layout before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Harden Admin Settings
use_cases.description: Review settings pages for capability checks, nonces, sanitization callbacks, and escaped output.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Release
use_cases.description: Check activation behavior, uninstall safety, assets, tests, and packaging before shipping a plugin update.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Plugin Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new plugin.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a WordPress plugin structure for [plugin goal]. Include bootstrap responsibilities, hook registration, folders, and required target versions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Secure Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Add an admin settings workflow for [setting purpose]. Use Settings API guidance, sanitization callbacks, capability checks, nonces, and escaped output.

prompt_templates.title: Review Lifecycle Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Review lifecycle behavior for [plugin path]. Check activation, deactivation, uninstall, rewrite flushing, migrations, and multisite concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WordPress plugin for release readiness. Check activation, settings saving, capability checks, uninstall behavior, tests, packaging, and documentation. Return prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: Request: Create a new plugin that stores one admin option.
output: A plugin structure plan with a single bootstrap and dedicated admin class.
A settings workflow using registration, sanitization, capability checks, and escaped output.
A verification checklist for activation, saving, and uninstall behavior.

output_examples.input: Request: Review a plugin before release.
output: A prioritized list of lifecycle, security, and packaging risks.
Specific checks for nonces, permissions, SQL safety, and request handling.
Recommended test and lint commands based on available project tooling.

output_examples.input: Request: Debug settings that do not save.
output: A focused diagnosis path for option groups, registration timing, capabilities, and nonce validation.
Likely failure causes mapped to the settings flow.
A short verification plan after the fix.

best_practices: Start by locating plugin entry files and target versions before editing.
Pair every nonce with a capability check for protected actions.
Run project tests, linting, and plugin activation checks after changes.
anti_patterns: Changing a full site repository before selecting the target plugin.
Trusting raw request data or escaping input instead of output.
Flushing rewrite rules or running migrations on every request.

faq.question: Does this skill create complete plugins from scratch?
faq.answer: It can guide a new plugin structure and implementation plan, but project details still drive the final code.

faq.question: Can it audit WordPress plugin security?
faq.answer: It covers common plugin security checks, including nonces, capabilities, sanitization, escaping, and SQL preparation.

faq.question: Does it require WP-CLI?
faq.answer: Not always. Some verification and debugging workflows may use WP-CLI when the project already supports it.

faq.question: What does the bundled scanner do?
faq.answer: It reads local PHP files to find WordPress plugin headers and reports detected plugin entry points.

faq.question: Can it handle multisite plugins?
faq.answer: Yes, if you provide the multisite context and target behavior before implementation or review begins.

faq.question: Does it replace official WordPress documentation?
faq.answer: No. It gives practical workflow guidance and points users toward official references for canonical details.
